\begin{definition}[Arithmetic machine state]
\lean{Complexity.BinArith.DState}
\label{Complexity.BinArith.DState}
\leanok
An arithmetic machine state consists of a list of rows of natural numbers together with

\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Encoding an arithmetic machine state]
\lean{Complexity.BinArith.encState}
\label{Complexity.BinArith.encState}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BinArith.DState, Complexity.BinArith.encMat, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $p$ be a natural number and let a state consist of a matrix $R$ and natural numbers
$d,m,r$. Encode $p$ in binary as the first component of a pair; its second component is
a nested pair encoding, in order, the matrix $R$, $d$, a string of $m$ true bits, and a
string of $r$ true bits. Each pairing doubles every bit of the first string, appends the
separator $01$, then appends the second string.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Determinant state update]
\lean{Complexity.BinArith.detStep}
\label{Complexity.BinArith.detStep}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BinArith.DState, Complexity.BinArith.elimRow}
Let $p$ be a natural number and let a state consist of a list of rows of natural numbers
and three natural numbers $(d,m,r)$. If $p<2$, or if the row list is empty, leave the
state unchanged. Otherwise, write the first row as $r_0$ and the remaining rows as $R$.
If $m\le r$, return the empty row list with all three numbers zero. If $m>r$ and the
first entry of $r_0$ (taken to be zero when the row is empty) is zero, move $r_0$ to the
end of $R$, replace $d$ by $d(p-1)$ modulo $p$ when $m$ is even and leave $d$ unchanged
when $m$ is odd, leave $m$ unchanged, and increase $r$ by one. In the remaining case,
replace every row in $R$ by its elimination using $r_0$ and the inverse power of its
first entry specified by exponent $p-2$, replace $d$ by $d$ times that first entry
modulo $p$, decrease $m$ by one, and set $r$ to zero.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Encoded determinant state update]
\lean{Complexity.BinArith.detWStep}
\label{Complexity.BinArith.detWStep}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BinArith.mapW, Complexity.BinArith.mod, Complexity.BinArith.mul, Complexity.BinArith.powMod, Complexity.BinArith.rowW, Complexity.BinArith.slC, Complexity.BinArith.slD, Complexity.BinArith.slM, Complexity.BinArith.slP, Complexity.BinArith.slR, Complexity.BinArith.sub, Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal, Complexity.isNilB, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Turing.pairEncode}
For a Boolean list $S$, define its updated encoding as follows. If the decoded parameter
is less than $2$, or the decoded row list is empty, leave $S$ unchanged. Otherwise, if
the decoded pivot count is at most the decoded counter, encode the same parameter
together with an empty row list and three zero counters. If the first entry of the first
decoded row is zero, move that row to the end of the remaining rows, update the
determinant component by multiplying it by the parameter minus one modulo the parameter
when the pivot count is even, and increment the counter; when the pivot count is odd,
leave the determinant component unchanged. In the remaining case, eliminate the first
row from the remaining rows using the modular power specified by exponent equal to the
parameter minus two, update the determinant component by multiplying it by the first
entry modulo the parameter, and remove one from the pivot count while resetting the
counter to zero.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial-Time Computability of a Binary Arithmetic Function]
\lean{Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_entryW}
\label{Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_entryW}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BinArith.entryW, Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_add, Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_mod, Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_mul, Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_slot2, Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_slot3, Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_sub, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.comp, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.pairEncode, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairFstD, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairSndD}
\difficulty{4}
For a bit string $w$, let $x$ and $y$ be the first components of the second and first
parsed pairs of $w$, respectively, and let $u$ and $v$ be the second components of those
pairs. Define $F(w)$ by taking the binary representation of
$\bigl((\max(\operatorname{val}(x)+\operatorname{val}(y)-((\operatorname{val}(u)\operatorname{val}(v))\bmod
\operatorname{val}(y)),0))\bmod \operatorname{val}(y)\bigr)$, where an unsuccessful pair
parse yields the empty string and $\operatorname{val}$ interprets the first bit as least
significant. Then $F$ is computable in polynomial time by a finite Turing machine.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Initial row construction]
\lean{Complexity.BinArith.initRows}
\label{Complexity.BinArith.initRows}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BinArith.decWords, Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD}
For a Boolean list $z$, form a list of rows by first decoding the second component of
$z$ into words. Decode each such word into entries, interpret each entry and the first
component of $z$ as natural numbers, and replace each entry by its remainder upon
division by the number represented by that first component.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Initial configuration encoding]
\lean{Complexity.BinArith.initW}
\label{Complexity.BinArith.initW}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BinArith.countW, Complexity.BinArith.mapW, Complexity.BinArith.rowModW, Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Turing.pairEncode}
For a Boolean list $z$, define its initial configuration encoding as a pair encoding of
the binary expansion of the number represented by the decoded first component of $z$ and
a second pair encoding. The second encoding consists of the rowwise modular
transformation of the pair encoding of that binary expansion with the decoded second
component of $z$, paired with an encoding of the singleton list containing true and the
pair encoding of the count of the decoded second component of $z$ with the empty list.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Encoding the initial arithmetic state]
\lean{Complexity.BinArith.initW_eq}
\label{Complexity.BinArith.initW_eq}

For every bit string $z$, the initial word constructed from $z$ equals the encoding of
the arithmetic state whose rows are obtained by decoding the second component of $z$
into words and then entries, reducing each entry modulo the natural-number value of the
first component of $z$. The state’s remaining parameters are $1$, the number of its

\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Determinant modular algorithm]
\lean{Complexity.BinArith.detModAlg}
\label{Complexity.BinArith.detModAlg}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BinArith.detWStep, Complexity.BinArith.initW, Complexity.BinArith.slD, Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal, Complexity.pairFstD}
For a finite list $z$ of Boolean values, define its output to be the empty list when the
integer represented by the decoded first component of $z$ is less than $2$. Otherwise,
start from the initial configuration determined by $z$, apply the transition rule
$(	ext{length}(z)+1)^2$ times, and return the decoded left component of the resulting
configuration.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Row-list state invariant]
\lean{Complexity.BinArith.LInv}
\label{Complexity.BinArith.LInv}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BinArith.DState}
Let $Q,K$ be natural numbers. A state consisting of a list $R$ of rows of natural
numbers and natural numbers $d,m,rc$ satisfies the invariant if $R$ has length $m$, that
length is at most $K$, each row has length at most $K$, every entry of every row is less
than $Q$, $d<Q$, and $rc\le m$.
\end{definition}

length of the shorter list is strictly less than $p$.

For natural numbers $p$ and $\mathrm{inv}$ and lists $\mathrm{piv}$ and $\mathrm{row}$
of natural numbers, the list obtained by eliminating the leading entry of $\mathrm{row}$
using $\mathrm{piv}$ has length
$\min(\mathrm{length}(\mathrm{row})-1,\mathrm{length}(\mathrm{piv})-1)$, where
subtraction is truncated at zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Preservation of the determinant-state invariant]
\lean{Complexity.BinArith.lInv_step}
\label{Complexity.BinArith.lInv_step}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BinArith.DState, Complexity.BinArith.LInv, Complexity.BinArith.detStep, Complexity.BinArith.length_elimRow, Complexity.BinArith.lt_of_mem_elimRow}
\difficulty{5}
Let $p,Q,K$ be natural numbers with $p\le Q$, and let $s$ be a determinant state
satisfying the invariant that its row count equals $m$, is at most $K$, every row has
length at most $K$ and entries less than $Q$, the stored value $d$ is less than $Q$, and
the counter $rc$ is at most $m$. Then one determinant step with parameter $p$ produces a
state satisfying the same invariant.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Binary length under an exponential bound]

Let $p,K,x$ be natural numbers. If $p<2^K$ and $x<p+2^K+2$, then the binary expansion of
$x$ has length at most $K+2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Determinant-preserving state invariant]
\lean{Complexity.BinArith.CInv}
\label{Complexity.BinArith.CInv}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BinArith.DState, Complexity.BinArith.matOfRows}
Let $p$ be a natural number and let $D_0$ be an element of the ring of integers modulo
$p$. A state consisting of a list $R$ of rows of natural numbers and natural numbers
$d,m,rc$ satisfies the invariant if $R$ has length $m$, each row has length $m$, every
entry is less than $p$, $d<p$, and $rc\le m$. In addition, every row with index $i$
satisfying $m-rc\le i<m$ has first entry zero (using zero when the row is empty), and
the determinant modulo $p$ of the $m$ by $m$ matrix formed from $R$, using zero for
missing rows or entries, multiplied by $d$ equals $D_0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[State measure]
\lean{Complexity.BinArith.dMeasure}
\label{Complexity.BinArith.dMeasure}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BinArith.DState}
For a state consisting of a row list and natural numbers $d,m,rc$, define its measure to
be $m(m+2)-rc$, with subtraction in the natural numbers.
\end{definition}

Let $p$ be a prime, let $D_0\in\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z$, and let $s$ be a
determinant-elimination state satisfying the invariant that its row list has the stated
matrix dimensions, all entries and the determinant accumulator lie in the range from $0$

step leaves $s$ unchanged.
